event.tilda_heart5.0.text: Sit, [player]. Right down. You look like you haven't slept in a week. I baked a dozen scones. Eat two.
event.tilda_heart5.0.why: frightened: the joke goes, the care gets exact and gentle

event.tilda_heart5.0.text: Sit a moment, [player]. You look tired around the eyes. I baked a dozen scones for a village that buys six.
event.tilda_heart5.0.why: uneasy: she notices the player's tiredness first

event.tilda_heart5.3.text: Nobody sits in a shop. They lean, they pay, the bell goes twice. You sat. ...Edmund sat there too. Same chair.
event.tilda_heart5.3.why: clue: the chair was Edmund's; a person to ask about

event.tilda_heart5.4.text: Same chair on Thursday? Come by daylight. I'll bake fewer scones. That's a lie, but a kind one.
event.tilda_heart5.4.why: frightened: a daylight rule slipped into the sign-off

event.tilda_heart2.0.text: Oh, [player]! Just the account I wanted. Come in out of the fog. I've something to hand over.
event.tilda_heart2.0.why: uneasy: the morning fog that will not lift

event.tilda_heart2.1.text: My mother's cauliflower gratin. Warm food, eaten early, and you sleep through. Don't thank me. Bring me a cauliflower someday.
event.tilda_heart2.1.why: frightened: feeding as protection, too exact

event.tilda_heart2.2.text: She wrote down one recipe in her whole life. Everything else she kept by heart. We were raised to keep things.
event.tilda_heart2.2.why: hint: a family of keepers, a custom of not writing down

event.hall_dance.3.text: Every name in this room, in the good chalk. All here. ...All here. Good. Nobody asked for credit, so I'm giving it.
event.hall_dance.3.why: frightened: she counts heads; the repeat is the distortion

event.hall_dance.3.text: Nobody asked for credit for any of this. So I'm giving it, in the good chalk, under every name. I counted twice.

event.hall_dance.10.text: Into the hall box, every coin. Except one. Marcus, that one's yours. Spend it on something that isn't wood. You've given it enough.
event.hall_dance.10.why: clue: 'wood' tips toward Harrow Wood; Marcus has given something

dlg.story.notes.tilda.1.text: ...Well. Now you know who's been doing it. Daylight only, mind. Nobody wants a knock after dark.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.1.why: uneasy: a rule about the dark, said like shop policy

dlg.story.notes.tilda.r2.text: A note, for me? ...You've been sleeping badly, haven't you. I'm keeping it. And keeping an eye on you.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.r2.why: frightened: Keeper gentleness that frightens more

event.story_notes_tilda.after.text: Signing a kindness is just sending a bill. Some of us keep the other account unsigned. ...Two more doors. Don't follow me.
event.story_notes_tilda.after.why: clue: a second, unsigned account; something kept

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.0.text: Mine is smiling. The birds have gone quiet this fall anyway. Still, a cheerful face never hurt a field.

dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.1.text: Dorian. Is that my prize pumpkin? I've been blaming the goats all week, and they're nervous enough already!
dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.1.why: uneasy: animals skittish, no harm shown

dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r0.text: Kindly, then. He's on the slate for a pie. ...And he keeps better count than anyone. Of trees, mostly.
dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r0.why: clue: echoes Dorian counting the trees

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.1.text: Marcus! Is that my prize pumpkin? I blamed the goats. They won't go near the back field lately, either.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.1.why: uneasy: animals avoid the wood side

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r0.text: Kindly. Fine. But he owes me a pie, and it'll be exact. He measures everything twice. Doors especially.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r0.why: clue: echoes the cellar door Edmund would not let Marcus oil

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r2.text: You and Marcus take the ends. I'll walk ahead. It's a face in a pumpkin, [player], nothing more. Breathe.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r2.why: frightened: the carved face lands wrong; she steadies the player

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.1.text: Felix. Is that my prize pumpkin? I blamed the goats! Everyone's jumpy this week, and now you!

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r2.text: You take the heavy end. Felix carries the excuses. I'll walk right beside you, [player]. Slowly.

event.festival_winter_lanterns.0.text: Lanterns up, everyone. Wait for the bell. One wish each. Some of us wish the same thing every year, and it keeps.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.0.why: clue: a yearly wish that is a duty

event.festival_winter_lanterns.0.text: Lanterns up, everyone. Not lit yet. Wait for the bell. Felix, I mean you. And none over the trees, please.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.0.why: uneasy: the wood mentioned as a custom

event.tilda_heart4.intro.text: Come around the counter. Nobody comes back here but me. Mind the cat. It's watched the back door all week.
event.tilda_heart4.intro.why: uneasy: an animal facing the wood

dlg.tilda.slate.0.text: This is the slate. Every small kindness in Wetherell, in chalk. The back is older debts. We don't turn it over.
dlg.tilda.slate.0.why: clue: an object to chase, the back of the slate

dlg.tilda.slate.r2.text: A promise. I'll write it small and hold it large. Now sit. You're pale, and the kettle's on.

event.tilda_heart6.intro.text: Turn the sign to Closed, would you? Just for an hour. Draw the blind on the wood side, too. Your chair's free.
event.tilda_heart6.intro.why: uneasy: a small household rule about the wood

dlg.tilda.hours.0.text: I count the stock at closing time. Four nights a year, I count people instead. Lately the street comes out short.
dlg.tilda.hours.0.why: clue: four nights a year, echoing the almanac dates

dlg.tilda.hours.1.text: A few of us keep something asleep in that wood. It costs. Last fall it cost Edmund. I wrote your letter anyway. What do you think?
dlg.tilda.hours.1.why: revelation (full): her clue scene; she confesses and asks; choices still answer 'stay or not'

dlg.tilda.hours.1.text: I tell myself Wetherell isn't shrinking. Then the lamps go out early, house by house. What do you think?
dlg.tilda.hours.1.why: uneasy: lamps lit early, then dark

dlg.tilda.hours.r0.text: Staying. ...Then stay near a lamp, on the dark nights. I'd like that on the slate in your handwriting.
dlg.tilda.hours.r0.why: frightened: the promise gets a condition

event.tilda_heart6.after.text: Said out loud, it weighs less. For both of us, I think. Turn the sign back, would you? And home before dark.
event.tilda_heart6.after.why: uneasy full: a Keeper's too-exact care closes the scene

dlg.tilda.card.0.text: Behind the flour sacks, in a very old tin, lies a recipe card in faded ink. The tin is colder than the room.

dlg.tilda.card.1.text: My mother's pumpkin pie. On the back, four dates a year, in her hand. I've never baked it. What if I get it wrong?
dlg.tilda.card.1.why: clue: the same four nights Edmund marked

dlg.tilda.card.r1.text: Safe. It's been kept safe for forty years. Keeping things is what this family does.

event.tilda_heart10.intro.text: Close your eyes. ...No, you're shaking. Keep them open, then. I've done something to the front of the shop.
event.tilda_heart10.intro.why: frightened: she will not ask a frightened player to close their eyes

event.tilda_heart10.give.text: Pumpkin pie, still warm. That's your farm on my sign, in paint. Supplier. Not kept in reserve, not on any list. I made sure.
event.tilda_heart10.give.why: revelation: the farm was the bargain; she has taken it off the list

event.tilda_friend.ask.text: Saturday stocktake, and the window's three sunflowers short. Something bright, please. The fog's sat on the street all morning.

event.tilda_friend.success.text: Three sunflowers! The window looks like noon, and we needed one. You're on the slate, under 'saved the display.'
event.tilda_friend.success.why: uneasy: the brightness is needed, not just pretty

event.tilda_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. I don't make a fuss, I make a large pie. Come in, and whatever you do, don't turn the slate over.
event.tilda_birthday.intro.why: hint: points at the back of the slate

dlg.tilda.birthday.r2.text: You'd mind it? That's the best present. Take the stool, keep the lamp lit. The cat will keep you company.
dlg.tilda.birthday.r2.why: frightened: she leaves the player the lamp and the cat

event.overheard_tilda_felix_1.l3.text: It's been in a bucket since dawn. It hasn't grown. Neither has anyone's catch, lately.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_1.l3.why: uneasy: the sea gone quiet, said in passing

event.overheard_tilda_felix_2.l4.text: Soup, a blanket, and 'Thin Ice' on the slate. Some warnings people walk past. I still write them.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_2.l4.why: clue: she writes warnings people ignore

event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l4.text: The pond always knows. Sit down, Felix. Tea for two, and the lamp on early.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l4.text: To old friends, dear. Eat up, Felix. ...And walk home with someone tonight.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l4.why: frightened: an oddly exact instruction to an unaware friend

event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l3.text: Flattery earns a ribbon. Imitation earns a bill. Copying the back earns a quiet word.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l3.why: hint: both keep a back side; Wren's reply still lands on 'ribbon'

event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l1.text: Six days at that counter. Save me a seat near the door? I may need to leave early.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l1.why: clue: Keepers leaving early, between two Keepers

event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3.text: One cup. Then back to the slate. No moon this week. I'll want my lamp.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3.why: hint: the new moon as a custom

event.overheard_tilda_juno_1.l2.text: Three clasps is two months of bread. The hinge is a tip. A bolt next, if you've one spare.
event.overheard_tilda_juno_1.l2.why: uneasy: she wants a bolt for her door

event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l2.text: Open one here and I'll stock your first shelf. Go farther, and... I'd understand. I'd post pie.
event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l2.why: clue: the shopkeeper who fears a shrinking village half wants Juno away

event.overheard_tilda_bram_1.l1.text: Bram. There's a pie crust on your bench. For the hinges, the shutters, and the brighter lamp.
event.overheard_tilda_bram_1.l1.why: uneasy: shutters and a brighter lamp

adds.text: And be home before the lamps tonight. Humor a shopkeeper. I like my accounts all in.
adds.why: the thing a Keeper does not quite say

adds.text: She kept a lamp on after closing, too. Some habits come with the shop.
...Doors open, lamps lit. And nobody walks home alone tonight. That's not advice.
adds.why: care too exact at the happiest moment

adds.text: Both face the field, mind. Never the wood. That's tradition.
...Mine's going up, not over the trees. Good. Hot cider in the shop after. Lamp's on.
adds.why: she watches where her lantern drifts

cuts.why: the Felix butter joke falls flat when the player is frightened; the added line fills the space

notes: Some variants carry an 'expression' field to keep the cozy beat's portrait; drop it if the compiler takes expression from the beat only.

dlg.tilda.hours.1 revelation (full, lore>=5, hearts>=6) is Tilda's confession; I treat heart 6 as her clue scene. The choices ('I'm staying' etc.) still answer it. Confirm with LORE.md that Tilda may name Edmund's cost here.
The back of the slate (heart4 clue, birthday hint, Wren overheard hint) is a new object to chase; it needs a payoff clue somewhere (Hazel or a Tilda later scene).
No variants on lines with {if} markup (scarecrows.after, heart4.after, heart8.after, heart10.thanks, birthday.after) to keep choice branching intact.
Overheard variants kept to 20 words or fewer; overheard_tilda_wren_2 and juno_2 left plain for contrast.
